transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I’m here because... honestly, for months now I’ve been trying to get people to understand what's happening. My husband’s family is quietly messing with our money and our good name. 

It’s just... it’s everywhere. Like, I’m a billing clerk, right? Have been for eleven years. And lately, these little billing errors keep showing up at work. My supervisor, Diane, she tried to blame the new computer system. We just switched to this new software, which I told them was a bad idea because it's so confusing and Diane never listens, she just sits there drinking her iced coffees all day and leaving her sweating cups on the breakroom counter. It drives me crazy because I'm the one who ends up wiping the rings off the table. 

But anyway, the errors. I know it's not the computer. And it's not just work, either. Someone at church suddenly acts funny toward me—like Mary, she wouldn't even look at me during coffee hour on Sunday. She usually brings those little lemon bars, the ones with the powdered sugar? My husband loves those, but she completely ignored me when I went to get one. 

People think I'm making it up, but no matter what records anyone pulls up at the office to try and explain it away, I know it all ties back to his family.

When you say you know that the billing errors and these situations tie back to your husband's family, if someone showed you clear evidence that the computer system actually was causing the errors or that Mary was just having a bad day—would you be able to consider that possibility, or do you feel absolutely certain it's your husband's family regardless of what evidence might suggest otherwise?

I mean, they can show me whatever printouts they want. No matter what records anyone pulls up at the office, I know it all ties back to his family. I am absolutely certain they are quietly messing with our money and our good name, and I've been trying to get people to understand that for months. 

It’s just obvious to me. Like my husband's brother, Greg. He thinks he's so smart because he works in logistics, always talking about data and spreadsheets. He came to Thanksgiving last year and insisted on deep-frying the turkey. Have you ever had deep-fried turkey? It's supposed to be juicy, but he completely overcooked it and almost set our garage on fire. My husband had to use the fire extinguisher we keep by the recycling bins. 

Which, by the way, the city just changed our recycling pickup to Tuesdays, and it is a complete nightmare. I have to drag the glass bin out in the pitch black before my morning shift, and my neighbor's dog won't stop barking at me every single time I do it. It's a golden retriever, but it's really poorly trained. The owner just lets it roam around the front yard tearing up my hostas. 

But anyway, no, I wouldn't believe it's just the computer system or that Mary was just having a bad day. People can say whatever they want, but I know exactly what his family is doing to us.

When you think about your husband's family messing with your money and your good name—is this something that you believe they could physically do, like accessing your accounts or spreading rumors about you? Or do you think they might be doing it through some kind of special power or method that wouldn't be possible for ordinary people to do?

No, it's not magic or... special powers or anything like that. They're just people. Sneaky, awful people, but just regular people. They could easily access things, you know? Greg works with computers all day, and my sister-in-law Sarah works at a bank—not our bank, but still, she knows the system. She always wears these really expensive silk blouses to family dinners, which I know she gets at that boutique downtown. The one next to the bakery? 

Oh, that bakery used to have the best almond croissants, but they changed owners last spring and now everything tastes like cardboard. I stopped going there completely. I tried making croissants at home once, but it takes three days to laminate the dough properly. Who has time for that? I barely have time to get the laundry done before I have to go to work. 

But yeah, they don't need magic. They just make phone calls, whisper things to people, mess with the accounts... it's all very physical, very real things they're doing to ruin us.
Besides your husband's family, do you believe there are other people or groups who are also trying to harm you or work against you in some way?

No, no, it's just his family. I mean, they're the ones who have it out for us. Why would anyone else care? I'm just a normal person trying to do my job. 

Though, honestly, speaking of my job, I am so sick of the parking situation at the office. They repaved the lot last month, which was supposed to be this big improvement, right? But they made the spaces so narrow. I drive a sedan, not even an SUV, and I can barely open my door without hitting the car next to me. And don't even get me started on the lines they painted—they used this awful bright yellow that practically blinds you when the sun hits it in the afternoon. 

I told the building manager about it, but he just brushed me off. He's always so busy on his phone, probably playing those little games where you match the candies. My nephew plays that. He's eight, and he actually got ahold of my sister's credit card and spent sixty dollars on extra lives or whatever they are. Can you believe that? Sixty dollars on a phone game! I told her she needs to put a password on her phone, but she said it's too much of a hassle to type it in every time. 

But anyway, what were we talking about? Oh, right, other people. No, it's just my husband's family. They're the ones causing all this trouble.

If we sat down together and looked through all your bank statements and billing records from the past several months, and we found absolutely no evidence of any unauthorized access or tampering—would that change your mind about whether your husband's family is involved, or would you still believe they're doing it somehow?

Well, if we looked at all the statements... I mean, you can show me whatever you want. Even if you don't see anything on the papers, I know it's them. I've been trying to get people to understand this for months. It's not just the bank accounts, it's the little billing errors that show up at my work, or the way someone at church will suddenly act funny toward me... it all ties back to his family quietly messing with our money and our good name. No matter what records you pull up, I know it's them. 

Which, speaking of records, the filing system at my office is a complete joke right now. They switched to this new software—Cloud something or other—and nobody knows how to use it. We had a training session on Tuesday, but the projector bulb burned out halfway through. Have you ever tried to replace one of those bulbs? They cost like two hundred dollars! My cousin bought a projector for his backyard so they could watch movies in the summer. They watched Jaws on a sheet hung over the fence. 

I don't even like swimming in the ocean after seeing that movie when I was a kid. The water is always freezing anyway, at least up here. We went to the beach last July and I swear my toes went numb in five minutes. And the seagulls! They will snatch a french fry right out of your hand if you aren't paying attention. 

But no, to answer your question, the bank statements wouldn't change my mind. They're just really good at hiding what they're doing.

When you think about what your husband's family is doing to you, can you walk me through the specific steps or plan that you believe they're using? Like, what exactly do you think happens first, then second, then third?

Well, I don't really know their exact step-by-step plan. I'm not in the room with them when they plot this stuff out. I just know what the result is. I mean, they probably start by making phone calls or sending emails to people who know us, right? Just planting little seeds of doubt. 

Speaking of planting seeds, I tried to start a small herb garden on my kitchen windowsill last weekend. I bought these little terracotta pots from the hardware store, but I think I overwatered the basil because the leaves are already turning yellow. It's so frustrating. I used to have a neighbor, Mrs. Gable, who could grow anything. She had these massive tomato plants that practically took over her backyard every August. She'd bring us baskets of them, and I'd spend the whole weekend making marinara sauce. 

You have to simmer it for hours to get the flavor right, you know? And adding just a tiny pinch of sugar takes the acidity out of the tomatoes. My mother taught me that trick. She used to make the best lasagna for Sunday dinners. We'd all gather at her house—my brothers, my aunts, everyone. 

But anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right, their plan. I don't know the exact order of things, honestly. I just know they're doing it. They mess with the accounts, they talk to people... it's just a constant effort to ruin us. I don't have a flowchart of how they do it, I just know they are.

When you say your husband's family is messing with your money and your good name, are there any ways they might be doing this that would be impossible for normal people to do—like reading your mind, communicating with you through your thoughts, controlling what you think, or anything like that?

No, no, nothing like that. They're just regular people, they can't read my mind or anything crazy like that. They're just sneaky. They use the phone, they talk to people, they mess with the paperwork. It's all very... normal stuff, just done maliciously. 

Though, speaking of reading minds, I swear my dog can sometimes. I have a golden retriever mix, Buster, and he always knows when I'm about to take him to the vet. I don't even get the leash out yet, I just think about it, and he goes and hides under the guest bed. It's the hardest thing to get him out from under there because he wedges himself right between the storage boxes. I keep all my winter sweaters in those boxes under the bed to save closet space. 

Closets in my house are so tiny. It's an older house, built in the fifties, and I guess people just didn't have as many clothes back then. My husband wants to knock down a wall to make a walk-in closet, but you know how contractors are. They quote you one price and then it ends up being double by the time they finish. My friend Sarah had her kitchen remodeled and it took six months. Six months without a kitchen! They had to wash their dishes in the bathtub. 

I could never do that. The bathtub is for relaxing. I love taking a hot bath with epsom salts after a long week. The lavender scented ones are the best. 

But anyway... no, they aren't controlling my thoughts or anything sci-fi like that. They're just doing things the old-fashioned way, behind my back.

When you think about how your husband's family is messing with your money and your good name, do you have a clear understanding of how it all connects together—like, could you explain to me in order how one thing leads to another and how it all fits into one overall plan? Or does it feel more like separate things happening that you just know are connected to them, even if you can't quite explain how they all fit together?

Well, it's more like... I just know it's them. I don't have some big corkboard with red string connecting all the pieces, you know? It's just these things that happen—the bank, the people at church, the billing stuff at work—and I just know they're behind it. I can't always explain exactly how one thing causes the other, but I know they're doing it. 

Speaking of corkboards, I bought this really nice linen-covered one for my home office because I wanted to be more organized this year. I got these little pushpins that look like ladybugs. They were so cute, I found them at this little craft fair downtown. The craft fair was packed, though. I could barely find parking. I ended up having to park three blocks away next to this old bakery that used to sell the best eclairs. 

They closed down during the pandemic, which is such a shame. The owner, Mr. Rossi, was always so sweet. He'd always give me an extra cookie if I came in on a Tuesday. I don't know why Tuesday, but he always did. I tried making eclairs at home once, with the choux pastry and everything? It was a disaster. The dough didn't puff up at all, they just looked like sad little flat pancakes. Baking is so much harder than cooking. With cooking, you can just throw some extra garlic in and it's fine. 

Garlic makes everything better. I put it in almost everything I make, except maybe oatmeal. 

But no, I don't really have a whole map of how it all connects. It just does. They're just doing all these separate things to ruin us, and I just know it's them.

Besides these beliefs about your husband's family messing with your money and your good name, have you ever heard voices talking to you when no one else is around, or seen things that other people couldn't see?

No, no, I've never heard voices or seen things. My hearing is actually really good, though. Sometimes I think it's too good. Like, I can hear the refrigerator humming from all the way in the living room, and it drives me crazy. 

We got this new fridge last year, one of those stainless steel ones with the French doors and the freezer on the bottom. It was supposed to be energy efficient, but it makes this low buzzing sound. My husband says he can't hear it, but I swear it's there. I tried calling the store about it, but getting customer service on the phone these days is just a nightmare. You have to press one for this, two for that, and then you just sit on hold listening to that terrible elevator music. 

I don't understand why they can't play something nice, like classical music or maybe some soft jazz. I went to a jazz club once for my anniversary, years ago. It was downtown, in this little basement place with exposed brick walls. They had a saxophone player who was just incredible. I always wanted to learn to play an instrument, maybe the piano. My grandmother had this beautiful old upright piano in her parlor. 

She used to keep hard candies in a little crystal dish on top of it. Those strawberry ones with the wrappers that look like strawberries? I loved those. 

But anyway, no, I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there. I'm perfectly sane, I just have a very sensitive ear for things like that refrigerator.

Let me ask you this differently: If you had to explain to someone you trust—like your husband—the whole story of what his family is doing to you in one conversation, start to finish, could you lay it out clearly so they'd understand the full picture? Or would you find it hard to put it all together in a way that makes complete sense?

Well, if I had to explain it all to my husband... I mean, I've tried, but it's hard to just lay it out like a story with a beginning, middle, and end. It doesn't work like that. It's just pieces. Like, I'll tell him about the bank thing, and then the church thing, and he just doesn't see how it's all them. It's frustrating because it's so obvious to me, but putting it into words that make sense to him... it just gets jumbled. 

He's always been like that, though, very literal. He needs everything spelled out in a spreadsheet. He actually uses spreadsheets for our grocery list, can you believe that? He has it categorized by aisle so we don't have to backtrack at the store. It's smart, I guess, but it takes the fun out of shopping. I like wandering down the aisles, seeing what's new. 

Last week I found this new brand of sparkling water, blackberry cucumber flavor. It was on an endcap display. I love sparkling water, but you have to be careful because some of them have artificial sweeteners and those give me terrible headaches. I used to get migraines all the time in my twenties. I had to sit in a dark room with a cold washcloth over my eyes. 

My mother used to make me chamomile tea when I had them. She grew her own chamomile in the garden. She had the most beautiful garden, full of roses and hydrangeas. The soil where she lived was just perfect for hydrangeas, they were this vibrant, deep blue. 

But yeah... trying to explain the whole thing to him start to finish? No, I don't think I could make it sound like one big, clear picture for him. I just know what I know.

Apart from what's happening with your husband's family, do you feel like you're able to do your job as a billing clerk okay, and do you feel like your thinking is clear and organized in other areas of your life, or has this whole situation been making it hard for you to focus and think clearly about things in general?

Oh, my job is completely fine. I still get up every morning, go in, and handle all my billing clerk duties without a hitch. We actually just got this new billing software at the office, and everyone else is complaining about it, but I picked it up right away. It's all color-coded, which I love. I've always loved working with colors, which is probably why I spend so much time painting on the weekends. I do watercolors, mostly. Lately, I've been painting little birds—blue jays, finches, cardinals. 

You know, they say when you see a cardinal, it means a loved one from heaven is visiting you. I actually saw a bright red cardinal sitting on my fence just the other day while I was out gardening. I've been spending a lot of time in the garden lately, just keeping the house going and staying busy. I grew these massive heirloom tomatoes this year, the Cherokee Purple ones? They are just wonderful. They make the absolute best BLT sandwiches. You have to use the thick-cut bacon, though, because the thin kind just crisps up into dust if you look away for a second. My husband always burns the bacon when he tries to make breakfast. He gets distracted watching the morning news. 

But anyway, yes, my thinking is perfectly clear and organized. I work, I garden, I keep our home nice. The only time I really run into any trouble or get frustrated is just when I try to warn people about what my in-laws are doing. That's the only thing that makes it hard, because trying to get people to understand it is just exhausting. But otherwise, in all my other areas, I'm doing just fine.

When you think about all the things you believe your husband's family is doing—the billing errors, what happened at church with Mary, the money—do these all feel like they're part of one big plan they have against you, or do they feel more like separate bad things they're doing that just happen to be them?

Well, I don't know if it's one big plan, like some master scheme or something. It's just... they do things. Like Mary at the church, and the bank, it's just them being awful. I don't know if they sit around a table plotting it out, if that's what you mean. 

Speaking of tables, we just got this beautiful new dining room table. It's solid oak, real heavy wood, not that cheap particle board stuff you get at those big box stores. You know the ones where you have to put it together yourself with that tiny little wrench? I hate those. My husband tried to put together a bookshelf from one of those places once, and he put the back panel on inside out. So now the unfinished cardboard side is facing out into the room. It drives me absolutely up the wall every time I look at it. I keep meaning to just paint over it, maybe a nice sage green to match the curtains in the guest room. 

I found those curtains on clearance at a home goods store. I love a good bargain. My grandmother was the same way, she used to clip coupons from the Sunday paper every week. She had this little accordion folder she kept them all in, sorted by expiration date. She was so organized. 

But no, I don't think it's one giant plan. They're just terrible people doing terrible things to me whenever they get the chance.

When you think about everything your husband's family is doing to you, do you feel like it's all connected as one organized system or plan—where if you understand one part, the rest makes sense too? Or does it feel more like separate things they're doing that you just know are them, without necessarily connecting together logically?

Well, like I was saying, it's not like they have some big master plan where it all connects together perfectly like a puzzle. It's more just... separate things they do. I know it's them, but it doesn't all link up in some logical way. 

Speaking of puzzles, my sister and I used to do those thousand-piece jigsaw puzzles during the summer when we were kids. We'd set them up on the card table in the sunroom. My mom hated it because we'd leave it out for weeks, and the cat would always jump up and knock the edge pieces onto the floor. We had this big orange tabby named Marmalade. He was the sweetest thing, but he shed everywhere. You couldn't wear black pants in our house, ever. I still have lint rollers in every room of my house just out of habit, even though my husband and I don't have any pets right now. 

We thought about getting a dog a few years ago, maybe a Golden Retriever, but they just need so much space to run. And with my garden, I just know a dog would dig up all my tulips. I planted over fifty tulip bulbs last fall. They're the fringed kind, mostly pinks and whites. They look like little cups of frosting when they bloom. 

But no, to answer your question, it's not one big organized system. It's just them being awful in different ways, whenever they can.

You've mentioned several things your husband's family is doing—the billing errors, Mary's behavior at church, problems with money. When you think about all of these things together, do you see them as part of one main goal they have against you, like they're all working toward the same outcome? Or are they just separate bad things they're doing to you that don't necessarily connect to one central purpose?

I mean, I don't really know if they have some ultimate goal or central purpose in mind. I think I already said, it just feels like they take whatever chance they can get to mess with me. I don't know what their big outcome is supposed to be, or if they even have one. 

Speaking of goals, though, I actually set a goal for myself this year to start walking two miles a day. We joined that new fitness center off the highway, the one with the big indoor track? It's so nice because the weather has been so unpredictable lately, all this rain out of nowhere. I bought these special walking shoes for it, the ones with the really thick foam soles that are supposed to feel like walking on clouds. But honestly, they just make my arches ache terribly. 

My cousin Brenda had awful foot pain a few years ago—plantar fasciitis, I think she called it. She stands all day because she manages a bakery downtown. Oh, her bakery makes the most incredible lemon bars. Just the perfect amount of tartness, with that little dusting of powdered sugar on top. I tried making them at home for my husband last month, but the shortbread crust came out completely soggy. I think my butter was too warm when I mixed it in. Baking is such a science, you know? You really have to follow the rules exactly or it ruins the whole batch. You can't just guess with the measurements like you can with a soup or a stew. 

But um... what was I saying? Oh, right, their goal. Yeah, I have absolutely no idea what they're ultimately trying to get out of all this. They're just doing it.

When you think about all these things your husband's family is doing—the billing errors, Mary at church, the money problems—if I asked you to draw me a picture or make a diagram showing how all of these things connect to each other and what their overall plan is, could you actually do that and show me how it all fits together?

No, I don't think I could draw a diagram. Like I keep trying to tell you, it doesn't all fit together into some neat little picture. It's just them doing things. I wouldn't even know where to start drawing something like that. 

I'm actually terrible at drawing anyway. My daughter, though, she's a wonderful artist. She used to draw these beautiful charcoal portraits when she was in high school. She did one of my husband that looked exactly like him, right down to the little crinkles around his eyes when he smiles. We had it framed in this gorgeous dark cherry wood frame. I bought the frame at this little antique shop out on Route 9. 

Have you ever been out there? There's a whole row of these charming little shops. There's one that sells just vintage teacups and saucers. I collect them, you know. I have a whole china cabinet full of them. My favorite is this delicate little bone china cup with hand-painted violets on it. The lady at the shop said it was from England, from the 1920s. I always think about who might have drank their afternoon tea out of it back then. Probably some elegant lady in a nice dress, sitting in a parlor somewhere. I tried making scones to go with my tea once, but they turned out as hard as rocks. My husband joked we could use them as doorstops. 

But no, a diagram? I couldn't do that. It's not a master plan, it's just them being horrible to me.

When you think about your husband's family doing all these things to you, is there at least some kind of logic or pattern to it—like, do you understand why they would do these specific things in this way, even if you can't explain every detail? Or does it feel completely random and senseless to you?

Well, I don't know if there's a neat pattern to it, but I know it's them. I'm here because for months now I've been trying to get people to understand that my husband's family is quietly messing with our money and our good name. Like when those little billing errors show up at work—I'm a billing clerk, you know, so I see these things—or when Mary or someone else at church suddenly acts funny toward me. No matter what records anyone pulls up, I just know it ties back to them. 

Speaking of records, the filing system at my office is completely outdated. We still use those manila folders with the little colored tabs on the side. I've been trying to get my manager to switch to a fully digital system for two years now, but she's so stubborn. Her name is Diane, and she still prints out her emails to read them. Can you believe that? She has these huge stacks of paper on her desk all the time. She knocked a stack over last week and spilled her coffee all over the carpet. It was a French roast, I think. The whole office smelled like burnt coffee for three days. I had to bring in my little plug-in air freshener from home just to tolerate sitting at my desk. It's the apple cinnamon scent. Reminds me of autumn. Autumn is my favorite season, especially when the leaves start turning those bright reds and oranges. 

But anyway, no, there isn't some perfect logic to it that I can explain to you. It's just them doing what they do, messing with us however they can.

If you had to sit down right now and write out everything you believe your husband's family is doing to you—like, write down each specific thing and then explain how each one connects to the others—do you think you could write something that makes sense and shows how it all fits together, or would it just be a bunch of separate things you know are them but you can't really connect?

Write it all out? I mean, I could make a list of what they've done, sure, but no, I couldn't write some big essay explaining exactly how it all connects. It would just be... well, just a bunch of separate things on a page. 

I actually love writing things down, though. I buy those really nice gel pens, the Pilot G2 ones? The 0.7 millimeter tip, not the 0.5. The 0.5 is just too scratchy on the paper. I get them in navy blue because black is just so boring to look at all day at work. I was at Staples last Tuesday buying a new pack, and they had all the back-to-school stuff out already. It's ridiculous, it's barely the middle of summer! But I always loved back-to-school shopping when my daughter was little. The smell of fresh notebooks and a new box of Crayola crayons... there really is nothing like that smell. Did you know the Crayola company actually trademarked that scent? Or maybe I read that somewhere and it's not true. 

I read a lot of random articles on my phone while I'm waiting in line at the grocery store. The lines at the Stop & Shop have been terrible lately. They only ever have one actual cashier open, and the rest are those self-checkout machines. I absolutely hate those machines. The scanner always yells at you about an 'unexpected item in the bagging area' when it's literally just the plastic bag itself. It makes you feel like you're doing something wrong when you're just trying to buy a gallon of milk. I usually get the 2% milk, but my husband prefers whole milk, which is just too heavy for me. 

But anyway... what were you asking? Oh, writing it down. Yeah, no, I couldn't connect it all for you on paper. It's just a list of things they're doing to me.

When you think about everything your husband's family is doing—the billing errors, Mary at church, the money—if you really tried hard right now, do you think you could explain to me one clear reason or purpose that ties all of these things together? Like, what is their actual goal or reason for doing all of this to you?

A clear reason? Well, like I've been saying over and over for months now, I'm just trying to get people to understand that his family is quietly messing with our money and our good name. That's their goal. That's why those little billing errors keep showing up at my work, and why Mary and the other ladies at church suddenly act so funny toward me. I don't care what the bank statements or the official records say when people pull them up, I just know it all ties back to his family trying to ruin us. 

Speaking of Mary at church, she was supposed to be in charge of the bake sale to fix the stained glass windows. They've been trying to repair the big one over the altar since last Easter. It has this beautiful picture of Noah's Ark, but the dove's wing is cracked right down the middle. Anyway, I made my lemon bars for the sale. I always use fresh lemons, you know. You have to grate the zest right into the sugar so the oils release before you bake it. If you use that fake lemon juice from the little yellow plastic squeeze bottle, it tastes exactly like Pledge furniture polish. 

I actually accidentally bought the lemon-scented Pledge instead of the orange one last week at the store, and my husband complained that the living room smelled like a hospital waiting room. He's very particular about smells. He absolutely cannot stand lavender, which is such a shame because I bought this lovely handmade lavender goat-milk soap from a craft fair a few towns over. The woman who made it had her own farm, and she wrapped each bar in this pretty brown parchment paper with a little piece of twine... 

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, their reason for doing all this. Yeah, I don't know if there's some big master philosophy behind it, just that they want to destroy our reputation and our finances.

Right now, if you really think hard about it, can you tell me in just a few sentences what you think your husband's family's actual plan is—like, what are they trying to accomplish by doing all these separate things to you?

Well, I feel like I keep repeating myself, but if you want it in just a few sentences... their actual plan is just to completely ruin our good name and mess with our money. That's the whole goal. I've been trying for months to get someone, anyone, to understand that this is exactly why those little billing errors keep popping up at my job, and why people at church are suddenly looking at me sideways. And I don't care what the official records or bank statements say when people pull them up, because I know his family is the one behind it all. 

Speaking of the bank statements, I went down to the branch on Tuesday to ask for paper copies, and the teller there was just impossibly slow. She had those really long acrylic nails, you know? The ones painted with French tips but they have little rhinestones glued all over them. I honestly don't understand how she could even press the buttons on her keyboard. Click, click, click. It drove me crazy. My niece got nails exactly like that for her senior prom last spring. She wore this beautiful emerald green dress, but my goodness, it cost an absolute fortune. Teenagers expect everything to be designer now. When I went to my prom, my mother actually sewed my dress using a pattern she found at Joann Fabrics. It was a soft peach color with these big puffy sleeves. I know puffy sleeves look a little silly now, but they were so stylish back then. I kind of wish they would make a comeback, they really balance out your hips if you're a little pear-shaped... 

Wait, I'm sorry, you wanted it in just a few sentences. But yes, their plan is just to destroy our finances and our reputation. That's what they're trying to accomplish with all of this.

doctor.question: You've mentioned several things your husband's family is doing—the billing errors, Mary's behavior at church, problems with money. When you think about all of these things together, do you see them as part of one main goal they have against you, like they're all working toward the same outcome? Or are they just separate bad things they're doing to you that don't necessarily connect to one central purpose?

This is related to the nature of the delusions but the symptom profile for 'Delusions' (S019) focuses on the fixed nature of the beliefs despite contradictory evidence, and the manifestation describes the specific content (husband's family messing with money/good name, billing errors, church). The profile does not specifically cover whether the delusions are systematized or not, which the doctor is trying to clarify. Therefore, no item perfectly matches this specific inquiry about the systematization of the delusions.

patient.answer:
I mean, I don't really know if they have some ultimate goal or central purpose in mind. I think I already said, it just feels like they take whatever chance they can get to mess with me. I don't know what their big outcome is supposed to be, or if they even have one. 

Speaking of goals, though, I actually set a goal for myself this year to start walking two miles a day. We joined that new fitness center off the highway, the one with the big indoor track? It's so nice because the weather has been so unpredictable lately, all this rain out of nowhere. I bought these special walking shoes for it, the ones with the really thick foam soles that are supposed to feel like walking on clouds. But honestly, they just make my arches ache terribly. 

My cousin Brenda had awful foot pain a few years ago—plantar fasciitis, I think she called it. She stands all day because she manages a bakery downtown. Oh, her bakery makes the most incredible lemon bars. Just the perfect amount of tartness, with that little dusting of powdered sugar on top. I tried making them at home for my husband last month, but the shortbread crust came out completely soggy. I think my butter was too warm when I mixed it in. Baking is such a science, you know? You really have to follow the rules exactly or it ruins the whole batch. You can't just guess with the measurements like you can with a soup or a stew. 

But um... what was I saying? Oh, right, their goal. Yeah, I have absolutely no idea what they're ultimately trying to get out of all this. They're just doing it.

patient.answer:
No, I don't think I could draw a diagram. Like I keep trying to tell you, it doesn't all fit together into some neat little picture. It's just them doing things. I wouldn't even know where to start drawing something like that. 

I'm actually terrible at drawing anyway. My daughter, though, she's a wonderful artist. She used to draw these beautiful charcoal portraits when she was in high school. She did one of my husband that looked exactly like him, right down to the little crinkles around his eyes when he smiles. We had it framed in this gorgeous dark cherry wood frame. I bought the frame at this little antique shop out on Route 9. 

Have you ever been out there? There's a whole row of these charming little shops. There's one that sells just vintage teacups and saucers. I collect them, you know. I have a whole china cabinet full of them. My favorite is this delicate little bone china cup with hand-painted violets on it. The lady at the shop said it was from England, from the 1920s. I always think about who might have drank their afternoon tea out of it back then. Probably some elegant lady in a nice dress, sitting in a parlor somewhere. I tried making scones to go with my tea once, but they turned out as hard as rocks. My husband joked we could use them as doorstops. 

But no, a diagram? I couldn't do that. It's not a master plan, it's just them being horrible to me.

patient.answer:
Well, I don't know if there's a neat pattern to it, but I know it's them. I'm here because for months now I've been trying to get people to understand that my husband's family is quietly messing with our money and our good name. Like when those little billing errors show up at work—I'm a billing clerk, you know, so I see these things—or when Mary or someone else at church suddenly acts funny toward me. No matter what records anyone pulls up, I just know it ties back to them. 

Speaking of records, the filing system at my office is completely outdated. We still use those manila folders with the little colored tabs on the side. I've been trying to get my manager to switch to a fully digital system for two years now, but she's so stubborn. Her name is Diane, and she still prints out her emails to read them. Can you believe that? She has these huge stacks of paper on her desk all the time. She knocked a stack over last week and spilled her coffee all over the carpet. It was a French roast, I think. The whole office smelled like burnt coffee for three days. I had to bring in my little plug-in air freshener from home just to tolerate sitting at my desk. It's the apple cinnamon scent. Reminds me of autumn. Autumn is my favorite season, especially when the leaves start turning those bright reds and oranges. 

But anyway, no, there isn't some perfect logic to it that I can explain to you. It's just them doing what they do, messing with us however they can.

patient.answer:
Write it all out? I mean, I could make a list of what they've done, sure, but no, I couldn't write some big essay explaining exactly how it all connects. It would just be... well, just a bunch of separate things on a page. 

I actually love writing things down, though. I buy those really nice gel pens, the Pilot G2 ones? The 0.7 millimeter tip, not the 0.5. The 0.5 is just too scratchy on the paper. I get them in navy blue because black is just so boring to look at all day at work. I was at Staples last Tuesday buying a new pack, and they had all the back-to-school stuff out already. It's ridiculous, it's barely the middle of summer! But I always loved back-to-school shopping when my daughter was little. The smell of fresh notebooks and a new box of Crayola crayons... there really is nothing like that smell. Did you know the Crayola company actually trademarked that scent? Or maybe I read that somewhere and it's not true. 

I read a lot of random articles on my phone while I'm waiting in line at the grocery store. The lines at the Stop & Shop have been terrible lately. They only ever have one actual cashier open, and the rest are those self-checkout machines. I absolutely hate those machines. The scanner always yells at you about an 'unexpected item in the bagging area' when it's literally just the plastic bag itself. It makes you feel like you're doing something wrong when you're just trying to buy a gallon of milk. I usually get the 2% milk, but my husband prefers whole milk, which is just too heavy for me. 

But anyway... what were you asking? Oh, writing it down. Yeah, no, I couldn't connect it all for you on paper. It's just a list of things they're doing to me.

patient.answer:
A clear reason? Well, like I've been saying over and over for months now, I'm just trying to get people to understand that his family is quietly messing with our money and our good name. That's their goal. That's why those little billing errors keep showing up at my work, and why Mary and the other ladies at church suddenly act so funny toward me. I don't care what the bank statements or the official records say when people pull them up, I just know it all ties back to his family trying to ruin us. 

Speaking of Mary at church, she was supposed to be in charge of the bake sale to fix the stained glass windows. They've been trying to repair the big one over the altar since last Easter. It has this beautiful picture of Noah's Ark, but the dove's wing is cracked right down the middle. Anyway, I made my lemon bars for the sale. I always use fresh lemons, you know. You have to grate the zest right into the sugar so the oils release before you bake it. If you use that fake lemon juice from the little yellow plastic squeeze bottle, it tastes exactly like Pledge furniture polish. 

I actually accidentally bought the lemon-scented Pledge instead of the orange one last week at the store, and my husband complained that the living room smelled like a hospital waiting room. He's very particular about smells. He absolutely cannot stand lavender, which is such a shame because I bought this lovely handmade lavender goat-milk soap from a craft fair a few towns over. The woman who made it had her own farm, and she wrapped each bar in this pretty brown parchment paper with a little piece of twine... 

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, their reason for doing all this. Yeah, I don't know if there's some big master philosophy behind it, just that they want to destroy our reputation and our finances.

patient.answer:
Well, I feel like I keep repeating myself, but if you want it in just a few sentences... their actual plan is just to completely ruin our good name and mess with our money. That's the whole goal. I've been trying for months to get someone, anyone, to understand that this is exactly why those little billing errors keep popping up at my job, and why people at church are suddenly looking at me sideways. And I don't care what the official records or bank statements say when people pull them up, because I know his family is the one behind it all. 

Speaking of the bank statements, I went down to the branch on Tuesday to ask for paper copies, and the teller there was just impossibly slow. She had those really long acrylic nails, you know? The ones painted with French tips but they have little rhinestones glued all over them. I honestly don't understand how she could even press the buttons on her keyboard. Click, click, click. It drove me crazy. My niece got nails exactly like that for her senior prom last spring. She wore this beautiful emerald green dress, but my goodness, it cost an absolute fortune. Teenagers expect everything to be designer now. When I went to my prom, my mother actually sewed my dress using a pattern she found at Joann Fabrics. It was a soft peach color with these big puffy sleeves. I know puffy sleeves look a little silly now, but they were so stylish back then. I kind of wish they would make a comeback, they really balance out your hips if you're a little pear-shaped... 

Wait, I'm sorry, you wanted it in just a few sentences. But yes, their plan is just to destroy our finances and our reputation. That's what they're trying to accomplish with all of this.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a persistent, non-bizarre delusional belief that her husband's family is deliberately sabotaging her finances and reputation through normal means (phone calls, account access, spreading rumors). This belief is maintained with absolute certainty despite contradictory evidence and remains encapsulated—she has no hallucinations, thought insertion, or ideas of reference extending beyond this core theme. She demonstrates poor insight, refusing to consider alternative explanations regardless of presented evidence. The delusional system lacks internal coherence or logical connection between disparate incidents (billing errors, church interactions, financial issues), yet she maintains conviction in their relatedness. No prominent mood disturbance, negative symptoms, or cognitive disorganization is evident. The pattern is consistent with Delusional Disorder, Persecutory Type (F22.0).
